dimensions.assessment: Directly affects federal banking supervisory agencies, including the Federal Reserve, Comptroller of the Currency, and the FDIC, as well as congressional committees.
dimensions.evidence: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System... Office of the Comptroller of the Currency... Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation

dimensions.assessment: Imposes new reporting, documentation, and economic impact analysis requirements on federal banking agencies regarding international standard-setting activities.
dimensions.evidence: include a description of the Board's interactions with global financial regulatory or supervisory forums

dimensions.assessment: Involves administrative costs related to preparing annual reports and congressional testimony, but does not state specific funding amounts or direct appropriations.
Amends statutory reporting requirements under the Federal Reserve Act, Revised Statutes of the United States, and the Federal Deposit Insurance Act.
dimensions.evidence: The seventh undesignated paragraph of section 10 of the Federal Reserve Act (12 U.S.C. 247) is amended

dimensions.assessment: Establishes permanent annual reporting and biannual testimony requirements for federal banking agencies.
dimensions.evidence: The Comptroller of the Currency shall make an annual report to Congress.

missing_information: Specific administrative cost estimates or staff hours required to compile the mandated reports are not provided.
importance_detail.rationale: H.R. 6550 requires federal banking supervisory agencies to provide detailed annual reports and biannual congressional testimony regarding their interactions with global financial regulatory or supervisory forums.

card.summary: The Main Street Capital Access Act modifies and lessens various banking regulations, adjusts capitalization requirements and asset thresholds for community banks and holding companies, and alters federal bank supervision, merger reviews, and resolution procedures.
